metadata.note: The Lehigh Valley's Auburn Branch -- the old Southern Central Railroad, which the LV financed and which completed a line from Athens, Pennsylvania north through Owego and Auburn to North Fair Haven on Lake Ontario in 1871. At 116.9 miles from Sayre with 29 stations it was the LV's long country branch, reaching from the anthracite main line at Sayre up across the Southern Tier and the hills east of the Finger Lakes to a Lake Ontario port. A December 15 1907 timetable called it the Lehigh and New York Branch of the Auburn Division. It was, in one historian's phrase, a gangly country cousin: passenger service was crude but the division stayed a serviceable railroad into the late 1930s. Passenger service to Fair Haven was discontinued in 1938 and to Auburn on 20 March 1948, which is where this map's coverage ends. The line was then dismantled piecemeal from 1937 to 1979; the Owego-Harford Mills portion survived by being sold to the Owego and Harford Railroad, and OSM still carries its name. This complements the LV main line and the Ithaca-area branches already on the map.

geometry_sources: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap end to end -- 124.8 mi against a documented 116.9 mi Sayre to North Fair Haven (+7%, partly because this trace ends at Fair Haven village rather than the North Fair Haven pier). NO straight-line legs and no bridged gaps: the whole route matched to connected track, much of it OSM's named 'Auburn Branch' and 'Owego & Harford'. Routed leg by leg through Sayre, Owego, Newark Valley, Berkshire, Richford, Harford Mills, Dryden, Freeville, Groton, Locke, Moravia, Auburn, Cato and Fair Haven; every leg came out within 34% of its straight-line distance and every station matched within 0.45 km. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 20 m, with the Auburn cut point preserved.
The 1938-1948 feature is the same trace cut at Auburn, 92.6 mi, against the documented Auburn milepost of 85.3.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways and speeds are estimates, not timetables. The 1871 completion date is for the Southern Central as a whole (Athens to North Fair Haven); the opening dates of individual sections are not sourced, so the full route is drawn from 1871. The Lehigh Valley's 1887 lease is used as the era boundary between the Southern Central and LV features, but the LV financed the line from the start, so the distinction is corporate rather than operational. The trace ends at Fair Haven village; the last 1.2 miles to the North Fair Haven pier are not drawn.

metadata.labelling: 2026-08-24: every feature in this file carries 'Lehigh Valley Railroad' at the start of its `line` field, which is what app.js shows in the hover tooltip, so LV routes are identifiable on the map without opening the data. Predecessor companies that were independent at the time are labelled '<Company> (Lehigh Valley predecessor)' rather than being relabelled as LV, because they were not yet Lehigh Valley in the years those features cover.
metadata.geometry_repair: 2026-08-24: removed four out-and-back spikes totalling 14.8 km from all three features; see geometry_quality. The Auburn one is the one to know about -- the original trace detoured onto New York Central trackage toward the NYC's Auburn station and back, which both inflated the mileage and put the Lehigh Valley on another company's rails through the town. Traced length went from 125.0 to 115.8 miles against a documented 116.9.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.geometry_quality: Geometry repaired 2026-08-24. The trace contained four out-and-back spikes where it ran up a spur or into a station and then retraced itself point for point. The worst was at Auburn: an 11.1 km excursion that left the Lehigh Valley alignment entirely and ran east onto ex-New York Central and Owego & Harford trackage toward the NYC's Auburn station, up to 1.27 km off the LV line, before mirroring itself back. Smaller spikes were removed at Sayre (0.7 km), Owego (2.3 km) and near Harford Mills (0.7 km). The through route now traces 186.3 km (115.8 miles) against a documented 116.9 miles Sayre to North Fair Haven -- down from 125.0 miles before the repair -- and every point through Auburn sits on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=LV (ways 95522193 and 173103424, both named 'Auburn Branch'). The cut-back feature ends 85.6 miles from Sayre against a documented Auburn milepost of 85.3.
